target_customer: Developers and companies in social, software, financial and fleet management that needed real-time messaging between web, mobile and server code
problem: Building real-time messaging and cross-language communication between clients and servers was hard. Flotype offered the open-source NowJS framework and the licensed Bridge middleware.
business_model: Open-source framework with paid licensed middleware and hosted service (Bridge, NowCluster)
product_category: Real-time messaging middleware and developer tools

founders.name: Darshan Shankar
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page. No bio found in opened sources.

founders.name: Sridatta Thatipamala
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page. No bio found in opened sources.

founders.name: Eric Zhang
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page. A Dealroom snippet mentions Amazon and small outsourcing work, but that page was not opened, so it is not recorded.

exit.reason: Cause and date not public. Dealroom and CB Insights mark the company closed or dead.

competitors.name: Pusher
competitors.what: Hosted real-time push service for web apps
competitors.funding_then: 1 million dollar seed from Passion Capital and Heroku founders in June 2011

competitors.name: PubNub
competitors.what: Hosted real-time messaging network, launched August 2010
competitors.funding_then: Series A of 4.5 million dollars came in March 2012

technical_complexity.rationale: Real-time RPC and message routing across languages with gateways and queues is standard distributed systems work but demanding for three founders, and Bridge needed multi-language clients.

defensibility.rationale: Open-source NowJS had no lock-in, and Bridge competed with other hosted and open-source real-time stacks such as Pusher and PubNub.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Rivals raised rounds in 2011 and 2012 and survived longer. Flotype is recorded as closed with no sale reported.

market_need_then: Node.js was growing fast in 2010 to 2011 and developers wanted real-time features. Salesforce, Andreessen Horowitz and Yuri Milner backing in January 2012 shows investor interest in the space.

branding.domain_note: flotype.com now redirects to a HugeDomains sale page (observed Nov 2026).

identity.voice_and_tone: Developer friendly, ease of use and simplicity (company description)

branding.brand_signature: NowJS, the open-source framework, was better known than the Flotype name
branding.community_and_virality: NowJS had a mailing list, IRC channel and several GitHub forks, and Ben Nadel blogged about it. No merch.

brand_strength.rationale: A developer niche brand. NowJS had some community use but there is no evidence the Flotype brand drove growth.

pivots.to: Flotype Bridge, cross-language RPC middleware for licensing or hosting
pivots.why: The announcement positions Bridge as a larger scope product than NowJS.

outcome_analysis: Flotype was a three founder YC W11 team that released NowJS and then Bridge, and raised a 1.4 million dollar seed in January 2012 from Andreessen Horowitz, Ignition, InterWest and Salesforce among others. The company is recorded as closed but no source states when or why, so the cause is not public and no failure factor is assigned.
notes: The 2012 seed is stated by Global Venturing (opened), and also by Xconomy and GeekWire in search snippets; GeekWire omits InterWest. The 20,000 dollar YC round in October 2010 rests on a single database (Dealroom); the Dealroom total of 1.42 million dollars over two rounds fits the two rounds. Sources conflict on the seed total (one aggregator gives 1 million). Website is dead (domain for sale). The PubNub source date is its launch date as given by Wikipedia and its funding line is dated after the batch. Pusher source is June 2011, about three months after the W11 batch. YC page says Bridge middleware licensing was already offered; the Bridge announcement post is dated April 2012.
